Rules for clear signage
This section covers how the desk handles it

Clear signs keep the Companion Animal Travel Desk easy to use and help travelers move through boarding without confusion. We post only simple, direct notices, and we keep them readable at standing eye level. Signs should match the current process, use plain language, and stay free of clutter. If a notice becomes torn, faded, or misleading, replace it right away and tell the next shift what changed.

At the desk, we guide travelers with calm directions and keep the path from check-in to handoff obvious. <<FACT F087>> Staff should never improvise alternate wording on signs or point travelers toward a different form when the posted one is in use. If a traveler asks for help, give a clear explanation in a friendly tone and make sure the display matches what the cabin team expects.

Incident reporting also needs clear placement, because people must know where to go when something is unusual. <<FACT F102>> Put the report notice where staff can see it quickly, and keep the wording short enough that no one has to guess what to do next. If an incident happens, stay steady, protect the traveler and animal first, and use the sign to support a clean handoff into the report process.

When in doubt, contact the shift coordinator or the duty manager for guidance and a fresh review of the signage.
